name: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
problem: Subquadratic alternatives to attention - linear attention, gated convolution, recurrent models, structured state space models - had not matched attention on language, and the paper diagnoses why: they cannot perform CONTENT-BASED reasoning, because their state transition and output are input-independent functions of the sequence.
mechanism: Selective state space models. Two changes to the SSM: (1) make the SSM parameters - the discretisation step size and the state matrix - FUNCTIONS OF THE INPUT, so the model selectively propagates or forgets information per token (this is the 'selectivity' and it is what enables content-based reasoning, but it also breaks the fast convolutional form); (2) to recover speed, design a hardware-aware parallel algorithm for the recurrent mode that scans the sequence in a memory-efficient layout. Mamba is then just these selective SSM blocks with no attention and no MLP.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract): 5x higher inference throughput than Transformers, with linear scaling in sequence length; Mamba-3B outperforms same-size Transformers and matches Transformers twice its size on language modelling. The throughput claim's baseline class is 'Transformers' generally, not a named engine, so treat 5x as the paper's own generalisation rather than a reproducible decode-tok/s figure.
